cards.text: Twenty YEARS, friend. That's how long Solomon spent building two houses: the house of the LORD and his royal palace. Now he has something for Hiram king of Tyre, the man who supplied him with cedar and cypress logs and gold for his every desire.

cards.question: Solomon gives Hiram king of Tyre twenty ___ in the land of Galilee.
Hiram goes out from Tyre to inspect his twenty new towns, and he's pleased with them.

cards.text: He is NOT pleased: “What are these towns you have given me, my brother?” That's the face of a man who opened the cookie box and found crumbs.

cards.question: Hiram gives Solomon's twenty towns a name, and it's still their name to this day. What does he call them?

cards.text: Oh, and Hiram had sent the king 120 talents of gold. ONE HUNDRED TWENTY TALENTS, friend, and Mother Miller got me for a quarter.

Next comes the account of the forced labor Solomon used to build the LORD's house, his palace, the supporting terraces, the wall of Jerusalem, and Hazor, Megiddo and Gezer. He also rebuilds more towns, plus store cities for his chariots and horses. And Gezer? Pharaoh king of Egypt had captured it, set it on fire, and given it as a dowry to his daughter, Solomon's wife. Some wedding gifts come in a box. This one was a whole city.

That's a LOT of building. And still living in the land are people who aren't Israelites, the ones the Israelites were unable to devote to destruction: Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites and Jebusites.

cards.question: Who does Solomon conscript to be his forced laborers?

answers.text: Men from every tribe of Israel

cards.question: Solomon also puts some of the Israelites into slavery.
Solomon doesn't consign a single Israelite to slavery. Why not?

answers.text: They serve as his soldiers and officers
They pay Solomon a yearly tax
They are needed to farm the land

cards.question: On Solomon's projects, the Israelites are also the chief ___ over the people who do the work.

cards.text: 550 supervisors in all! Meanwhile Pharaoh's daughter moves up from the City of David into the palace Solomon built for her.

cards.question: As soon as Pharaoh's daughter moves into her palace, Solomon builds the supporting ___.

cards.text: Through all the building, there's worship too. On the altar he built for the LORD, Solomon offers burnt offerings and peace offerings, burning incense with them before the LORD.

cards.question: Solomon brings these offerings before the LORD three times a year.

cards.text: So he completed the temple. And now King Solomon assembles a fleet of ships at Ezion-geber, near Eloth in Edom, on the shore of the Red Sea.

cards.question: Hiram king of Tyre sends his servants, sailors who know the sea, to serve in Solomon's fleet.
Hiram's sailors and Solomon's servants set sail together. Where do they go to bring back gold?

cards.text: They bring back gold from Ophir, 420 talents of it, and deliver it to Solomon. FOUR HUNDRED TWENTY TALENTS, friend, and here I am feeling fancy about one gold base.

findings.problem: Solomon appears for the first time with no word on who he is. The card never says he's king of Israel, even though verse 11 calls him King Solomon. Hiram gets an introduction (king of Tyre), but Solomon doesn't.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The joke compares Hiram's 120 talents of gold to the quarter Mother Miller paid for Papa Dorin. That makes the gold sound like a purchase price, likely for the twenty towns. Verse 14 doesn't say how the gold connects to the towns or the earlier supplies.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The right answer, "The descendants of those peoples," points back to the list of peoples on card 8, which is no longer on screen. Without that card, the baker can't tell who "those peoples" are.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "Men from every tribe of Israel" is false in this passage, since verses 20 to 22 name non-Israelites as the forced laborers. But 1 Kings 5:13 says Solomon conscripted forced laborers from all Israel, 30,000 men. A baker who knows that verse could argue this wrong answer is right.
findings.question: Should a wrong answer be replaced when it's false in the passage but true somewhere else in the Bible, especially in the same book just a few chapters earlier? The rules only require wrong answers to be false anywhere in the passage.

findings.problem: "Meanwhile" says Pharaoh's daughter moves into her palace at the same time as the supervisors' work. Verses 23 and 24 give no such timing.

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: Card 7 already lists "the supporting terraces" among Solomon's projects (verse 15). That gives away the blank on card 14, "Solomon builds the supporting ___." The baker can match the earlier wording instead of reasoning it out.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: "Through all the building, there's worship too" places Solomon's offerings during the building years. Verse 25 says only "three times a year" and doesn't link the offerings to the building period.

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: "These offerings" points back to card 15, which is no longer on screen. The question should name the burnt offerings and peace offerings.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.
